source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15 ("Keady"); also the Armagh Guardian, 8 May 1936, p. 3 ("No fight at Keady")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed, no poll; every name checked against the page image

note: Declared elected; the first five were retiring members. The paper gives the new council as seven Nationalists and two Unionists (Martin and Ewart had sat as Unionists). Returning officer P. J. Carbery. The January 1935 elections had been put back to May 1936. Polling day was the ordinary day of election, Friday 15 May 1936 (Belfast Gazette, 19 June 1936, p. 221; the Portadown Times of 15 May 1936, p. 5, writes of "to-day's elections").
